messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the 3fa2b7c merge we started seeing steady memory growth on longctx machines during canary. Rollout halted. Repro on staging shows KV heap drift that correlates with warmup bursts at batch boundaries.
jin: Can you paste the root logs and which commit you rolled?
alex: Rolled commit 3fa2b7c -> feature:kernel-router/batching-v2. Logs:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] pod/gpu-12 kernel-router: selected kernel=fast_attention_v2 for model=redwood-13b seq=4096
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] runtime/kvcache: warmup: slab_bucket=18 prefetch=on warmup_ts=1611
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] runtime/kvcache: heaplet_usage=1.2G -> 1.9G -> 2.6G (growing)
[2026-03-10T14:02:14Z] oom: process killed due to RSS > 24G
```
jin: OK, that warmup pattern is suspicious. Did kernel routing change eviction semantics? 3fa2 touched routing + autobatch.
loren: It did — routing now pins some slabs for fast kernels during first N requests to avoid cold misses. Might be a warmup "heartbeat" we introduced. Pinning + longer seq lengths = heap drift.
sara: CI also flagged a perf regression on the PR: longctx_memory_pressure_latency_test failed (latency regress > 12%). ci-bot: test/longctx_memory_pressure_latency_test FAILED on PR 3fa2b7c (regression detected).
infra-bot: Deploy hold applied to rollout/redwood-13b/canary by ops at 2026-03-10T14:10Z :no_entry_sign:
alex: Reproduced locally with small harness: seq_len=4096, batch stove=autobatch-v2, run 1000 requests -> RSS climbs steady until OOM. Reproducer attached (link to internal gist).
jin: Can you run a pprof heap snapshot at T+200 and T+800? Also perf top while warmup is happening.
alex: Ran pprof snapshots. Commands: `curl http://staging:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap.t0` then again at t+600 `> heap.t1`. Heap allocs point to kvcache::prefetch_slab::fill_entry and kvcache::evict_windows::deferred_mark. Perf top shows heavy stacks in nvcomp related memcpy + kernel selection path.
loren: That deferred_mark path is new — we changed eviction to be epoch-aligned with kernel pinned slabs. If the epoch advance is gated by batch boundary, eviction doesn't reclaim until much later. Sequence-length sensitive workloads will force many slabs to be pinned for the fast kernel.
sara: Any quick mitigations we can flip in config before a revert?
loren: Two options: 1) turn off slab pinning: `runtime.flags.disable_kernel_pin=true` (hot fix, low risk), or 2) reduce pin window: `runtime.flags.kv_pin_window_ms=50` (still experimental). 1 is safer.
jin: I tested disable_kernel_pin locally — memory growth stops, RSS stabilizes ~6G under same load. Latency stay within SLO.
alex: Good. I'll push a patch to canary config and re-run smoke. If that stabilizes, we can continue rollout while we bisect the kernel-routing changes.
loren: For bisect: start with 3fa2b7c^ and walk commits touching router and autobatch. I suspect the change in `evict_windows` interaction with `kernel_pin` is the root.
sara: Make sure to include a CI perf job that runs longctx_memory_pressure_latency_test with seq_len=4096 for 10k requests — gate on that before re-rolling.
alex: Will open PR to update canary config and add the CI job. Also creating a bisect checklist and assigning to @loren/@jin.
ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered for canary-config patch #1209 — smoke & longctx tests queued.
infra-bot: Canaries paused, ops confirmed hold until we confirm canary stability.
loren: Next steps: (1) patch canary to disable kernel pinning (2) run perf + heap snapshots (3) bisect to find offending commit and prepare a targeted revert or fix (4) hard gate CI test. I'll start the bisect tomorrow morning.
alex: Thanks everyone — setting rollout hold + incident note. I'll paste graphs and heap diffs once available. :thumbsup:
